name: ExpeL

paper.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners

construction.unit: two kinds: successful trajectories from training tasks, and short natural-language insights
construction.kept_as: trajectories stored as they ran; insights written by an LLM from many trajectories
construction.processing: ReAct + Reflexion (up to 3 retries) on training tasks fills an experience pool; GPT-4 then compares failed and successful attempts of the same task and groups of L successes, editing a list of insights
construction.writer: gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 gathers trajectories; gpt-4-0613 writes insights

organization.structure: experience pool of trajectories + a ranked flat list of insights with importance counts
organization.stores: Faiss vector store of successful trajectories (keyed by task text); insight list
organization.index: all-mpnet-base-v2 embedding of the task text, kNN in Faiss

management.operations: insights: ADD / EDIT / UPVOTE / DOWNVOTE by the insight LLM (AGREE / REMOVE in code), with importance counts
management.conflicts: the LLM can edit or downvote an insight a new comparison contradicts; an insight whose count reaches 0 is deleted
management.forgetting: insight deleted at count 0; no forgetting of trajectories

retrieval.query: the evaluation task's text (question, instruction or goal)
retrieval.candidates: kNN by inner product on task embeddings over successful training trajectories (code: same ALFWorld task type, k × 4 candidates)
retrieval.selection: top-k by task similarity; code skips trajectories longer than the longest hand-written example, the same task and duplicates
retrieval.budget: k = 6 HotpotQA, 2 ALFWorld, 2 WebShop few-shot trajectories; all insights

use.context: task instruction + k retrieved successful trajectories as few-shot + full insight list + task + current trajectory
use.reasoning: ReAct actor (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613), one attempt per evaluation task

classify.note: Two stores: trajectories are retrieved by embedding kNN on the task text; the insight list is always read in full. Consolidation is the LLM editing the insight list offline.

stages.ingestion: On training tasks a ReAct agent with Reflexion retries each failed task up to 3 times; every trajectory, successful or failed, enters the experience pool.
stages.construction: Successful trajectories are kept as they ran. An insight LLM (gpt-4-0613) reads fail/success pairs of the same task and chunks of L successful trajectories (L = 8, or 4 on WebShop) and proposes operations on the insight list.
stages.organization: Successes are indexed in Faiss by an all-mpnet-base-v2 embedding of their task text; insights form one list ordered by importance count.
stages.update: ADD starts an insight at count 2; UPVOTE and EDIT add 1; DOWNVOTE subtracts 1 (code: 3 when the list is over its cap); an insight at 0 is removed.
stages.retrieval: For a new task, the top-k successful trajectories by task-text similarity become the few-shot examples (k = 6 HotpotQA, 2 ALFWorld and WebShop); the whole insight list is added without search.
stages.answer: A ReAct actor (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613) solves the evaluation task in one attempt with these examples and insights in its prompt.
stages.learning: No weight updates: learning is the offline insight extraction plus the growing pool of retrievable successes. Insights can be carried from HotpotQA to FEVER by rewriting them with GPT-4 and target-task examples.

summary: An agent gathers trial-and-error experience on training tasks, has GPT-4 distil it into a vote-weighted list of insights, and at test time solves new tasks in one try using all insights plus its most similar past successes as few-shot examples.
notes:
Venue: AAAI 2024 main track, verified on ojs.aaai.org (AAAI vol. 38 no. 17, pp. 19632-19642); the arXiv v3 PDF also carries the AAAI 2024 copyright line.
DESIGN: §4.1-4.3, Alg. 1-3, App. D-E (Table 4). Management vocabulary: the paper says UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE, the code says AGREE/REMOVE. Retrieval details (task-type filter, ×4 candidate buffer, length filter) come from the code only. Main results exist only as bar labels in Fig. 5 (read from the rendered PDF page).

sources.code_note: The code was first released on 2024-01-23 (after the AAAI version); later commits only edit the README and delete ALFWorld data folders. HEAD e41ec9a (2024-12-20) is used. Run commands with per-benchmark settings are in README L202-L241.

headline: Two memories: raw successful trajectories, retrieved by task similarity as few-shot examples, and a short list of GPT-4-written insights that is always read in full.
Everything is built offline from one half of the benchmark tasks and tested on the other half with a single attempt.

units.name: Successful trajectory
units.role: a solved training task, reused as an in-context example
units.made_by: ReAct + Reflexion agent during experience gathering

fields.name: task text
fields.what: the question or instruction; the only text that is embedded for retrieval

fields.name: trajectory
fields.what: thoughts, actions and observations as run; the shortest success of a task is the one shown

fields.name: thought / step / action / reflection docs
fields.what: also indexed, used only by alternative fewshot strategies (the paper's reason-similarity ablation)

units.name: Failed trajectory
units.role: a failed attempt at a training task

fields.name: trajectory
fields.what: compared with a success of the same task during insight extraction; never retrieved

units.name: Insight
units.role: one general rule for the task family

fields.name: rule text
fields.what: one sentence of advice, e.g. to reassess or to try other search terms
fields.src: paper §4.2, App. G; code agent/expel.py L404-L412

fields.name: importance count
fields.what: starts at 2; orders the list and deletes the rule at 0; not shown to the actor

write.how: ReAct on each training task; on failure Reflexion reflects and retries, reflections concatenated
for each training task with a success, GPT-4 sees the success and each failed attempt plus the current insight list and outputs operations
successful trajectories are split randomly into chunks of L and GPT-4 edits the insight list from each chunk
parse ADD / EDIT / AGREE / REMOVE; ADD = 2, AGREE and EDIT +1, REMOVE −1 (−3 when the list is 5 over the cap); drop at 0; sort by count
embed the task text of every successful trajectory (and of the hand-written few-shots) with all-mpnet-base-v2 into Faiss

read.how: Faiss kNN on all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings; ALFWorld restricted to the same task type
walk candidates in order; skip the same task, duplicates and trajectories longer than the longest hand-written example; stop at k
the whole numbered insight list is inserted before the task, with a benchmark-specific header

answer_context.sees: k successful past trajectories as few-shot, all insights, the task and the current trajectory
answer_context.format: instruction with the k trajectories as examples, then e.g. "The following are some experience you gather on a similar task..." and the numbered insights, then the task

compression.what: insights vs the experience they summarise
compression.basis: Not reported. The list is capped by prompt (10 or 8 rules in the README runs) whatever the number of trajectories.

paper_vs_code.paper: 'four-fold validation' (§5.1), described as training on one half and evaluating on the other, and vice versa (App. D.1)

paper_vs_code.code: REMOVE subtracts 1, or 3 once the list holds 5 more rules than the cap; the prompt also discourages ADD when the list is full

paper_vs_code.paper: top-k successful trajectories by task similarity
paper_vs_code.code: only the same ALFWorld task type; hand-written few-shots are in the pool; trajectories longer than the longest hand-written example are skipped; WebShop drops ones with invalid actions
default agent.llm is gpt-3.5-turbo; the README runs set agent.llm=gpt-4

open_questions: Training and evaluation tasks are two halves of the same small sets (100 HotpotQA, 134 ALFWorld, 100 WebShop), so retrieved successes are near neighbours by construction; how this transfers to a different task distribution is only probed by the HotpotQA → FEVER insight transfer.
ExpeL reads more context than ReAct (4,310 vs 1,320 tokens per HotpotQA trajectory, Table 6); no baseline gets the same budget of hand-picked examples.

discussion.takeaway: Letting an agent practise on training tasks and then reuse both distilled insights and its own most similar successes improves single-attempt success on unseen tasks without any fine-tuning. The two parts help different domains: insights matter more on HotpotQA, retrieved examples on ALFWorld.

claims.claim: Learning from experience beats the ReAct and Act baselines.
claims.evidence: Success rate: HotpotQA 39 vs 28 (ReAct), ALFWorld 59 vs 40, WebShop 41 vs 35 (Fig. 5).
Insights-only / retrieve-only: 36 / 31 on HotpotQA, 50 / 55 on ALFWorld, 37 / 38 on WebShop; both together are best (Fig. 5, §5.2).

claims.claim: Cross-task learning without retries can match Reflexion's retries.
claims.evidence: HotpotQA 39 vs Reflexion 40 at R3; ALFWorld 59 vs 54 at R3; WebShop 41 is below Reflexion's 43-48 (Fig. 5, §5.2).

claims.claim: More and more diverse experience helps.
claims.evidence: Insights from the few-shots alone give no gain over ReAct; gathering with Reflexion beats gathering with ReAct only (Fig. 6, §5.6).
HotpotQA insights adapted to FEVER: 70 vs 63 (ReAct) and 65 without target examples (Table 1).

Learned insights 39.0 beat hand-crafted 32.0; adding reflections drops to 29.0; gpt-3.5 insights 32.0; task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs 48.5 reasoning similarity and 42.5 random on ALFWorld (Table 3).

limits: Only textual observations; images would need a VLM or captioner.
Only closed-source API LLMs were tested.
All insights fit in the context window here; lifelong use would need insight retrieval.
Prompting methods lack the theory behind RL, which may affect how good the resulting policy is.
reading: Insights are never retrieved: the whole list goes into every prompt, and the README caps it at 10 (8 on WebShop) through the extraction prompt, so the insight memory is small by design.
Retrieval matches only the task text; the trajectory, thoughts and outcomes are not compared with the new task.

Evaluation uses gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 while the insights come from gpt-4-0613, so part of the gain may be distilled GPT-4 advice; the gpt-3.5 insights ablation (32 vs 39 on HotpotQA) shows the size of that effect on one benchmark.
Reflexion baselines (R1-R3) retry the same test task with a correctness signal; ExpeL gets one attempt, so the comparison favours Reflexion's access to test feedback rather than ExpeL.
Main results are only given as bar labels (integers) and standard-error arrows in Fig. 5; Tables 2-3 and 5 give finer numbers for some settings.

abstract.text: ExpeL is an LLM agent that learns from its own experience without changing model weights. It first attempts a set of training tasks, retrying failures with self-reflection, and stores the resulting trajectories. An LLM then distils insights from contrasts between failures and successes and from groups of successes. At test time the agent solves each new task once, prompted with these insights and with its most similar past successes; the authors report consistent gains over ReAct on HotpotQA, ALFWorld and WebShop and positive transfer to FEVER.
